This report summarises the prepared observations. Run `scripts/prepare_report_figures.py descriptives` after `scripts/prepare_data.py` to regenerate the tables and figures. The figures are cached under `docs/descriptive/figures/` and are not version-controlled.
:::

The report describes the number of observations, age coverage and vocabulary counts in the prepared pool. The [technical report](../report/) and [model pages](../models/) describe the fitted models.

Each row represents one parent-report checklist administration for one child at one age. It records words understood, spoken and, where available, signed. Counts are harmonised onto an 810-word reference scale. Repeatedly measured children contribute several rows. The table gives the current prepared counts by study. `us_03` contributes comprehension only because its expressive field combines speech and sign; a spoken-only count cannot be recovered from it (see [the source note](../../data/vocab_data_us_03.md)).

## Study inventory

```{python}
#| label: tbl-inventory
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Per-study data inventory (observed counts). Obs. = checklist administrations; Children = distinct subjects; medians are of the observed word counts (blank where a study records no such measure)."
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

_p = Path("figures/dataset_summary_ds.csv")
if not _p.exists():
    _out = pd.DataFrame({"note": ["Run scripts/prepare_report_figures.py descriptives first."]})
else:
    _d = pd.read_csv(_p)

    def _rng(lo, hi):
        return f"{int(round(lo))}–{int(round(hi))}"

    def _med(v):
        return "" if pd.isna(v) else f"{v:.0f}"

    _out = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Study": _d["study"],
            "Obs.": _d["n_observations"].astype(int),
            "Children": _d["n_subjects"].astype(int),
            "Age (mo)": [_rng(a, b) for a, b in zip(_d["age_min"], _d["age_max"])],
            "Understood n": _d["understood_n"].astype("Int64"),
            "Understood med.": _d["understood_median"].map(_med),
            "Spoken n": _d["spoken_n"].astype("Int64"),
            "Spoken med.": _d["spoken_median"].map(_med),
            "Signed n": _d["signed_n"].astype("Int64"),
        }
    )
    _total = {
        "Study": "All",
        "Obs.": int(_d["n_observations"].sum()),
        "Children": int(_d["n_subjects"].sum()),
        "Age (mo)": _rng(_d["age_min"].min(), _d["age_max"].max()),
        "Understood n": int(_d["understood_n"].sum()),
        "Understood med.": "",
        "Spoken n": int(_d["spoken_n"].sum()),
        "Spoken med.": "",
        "Signed n": int(_d["signed_n"].sum()),
    }
    _out = pd.concat([_out, pd.DataFrame([_total])], ignore_index=True)
_out
```

Studies differ in sample size, age coverage and measurement. These differences motivate study effects in the models. The effects cannot correct every difference in recruitment or measurement.

## Vocabulary by age

The plots show all retained observations over the pool's age range, including children measured once. Colour identifies the study. The red band spans the 25th to 75th percentiles in each six-month age group with at least five observations. This describes the middle half of the observed counts, not uncertainty about the average. Check the number and mix of studies before interpreting an age pattern, especially at older ages.

![Words understood by age, coloured by study, against the pooled interquartile band](figures/observations_age_understood_ds.png){#fig-understood-age .lightbox fig-align="left"}

![Words spoken by age, coloured by study, against the pooled interquartile band](figures/observations_age_spoken_ds.png){#fig-spoken-age .lightbox fig-align="left"}

### The typically-developing reference pool by age

The Wordbank pool has many observations at each month of age. Each violin shows that month's count distribution, clipped to the observed range. The line and band show the pooled median and interquartile range. Comprehension is available only from forms that record it, so the two panels have different age coverage.

![Words understood by age (typically developing), monthly distributions](figures/violins_age_understood_td.png){#fig-understood-age-td .lightbox fig-align="left"}

![Words spoken by age (typically developing), monthly distributions](figures/violins_age_spoken_td.png){#fig-spoken-age-td .lightbox fig-align="left"}

## Individual trajectories (repeated measures)

Each line joins one child's visits on the same checklist form. Lines do not join visits across forms because a changed item list could look like development. The background median, mean and interquartile range use all observations in the age window, including children measured once. The Down syndrome panels show ages 8–72 months.

![Words understood by age, individual repeated-measures trajectories (Down syndrome), by study](figures/repeat_measures_age_understood_ds.png){#fig-rm-understood .lightbox fig-align="left"}

![Words spoken by age, individual repeated-measures trajectories (Down syndrome), by study](figures/repeat_measures_age_spoken_ds.png){#fig-rm-spoken .lightbox fig-align="left"}

Differences between lines can reflect child differences, assessment variation and study effects. A change between visits is not, by itself, an estimate of a child's underlying learning rate.

### The typically-developing reference pool

The Wordbank panels use the 8–30 month admission window and three-month age groups. The comprehension panel ends where its forms do. Repeated measurements are concentrated in a few studies, so changes in pooled age summaries can also reflect changes in the study mix.

![Words understood by age, individual repeated-measures trajectories (typically developing), by dataset](figures/repeat_measures_age_understood_td.png){#fig-rm-understood-td .lightbox fig-align="left"}

![Words spoken by age, individual repeated-measures trajectories (typically developing), by dataset](figures/repeat_measures_age_spoken_td.png){#fig-rm-spoken-td .lightbox fig-align="left"}

## Words understood versus words spoken

Plotting spoken against understood shows the two are strongly coupled, and that observations sit largely **on or below the diagonal**: children generally say no more than they understand, and usually fewer. The joint models represent spoken counts conditionally on understood counts. The default loader also masks comprehension when it is contradicted by production, so the prepared scatter is not an independent test of that nesting assumption.

![Words understood versus words spoken, coloured by study](figures/scatter_understood_spoken_ds.png){#fig-us .lightbox fig-align="left"}

## Signed vocabulary

Only some studies record signing, and their response options differ. Read the [source notes](../../data/readme.md) before comparing their counts. VG14, VG15 and the models derived from VG15 examine signing alongside comprehension and speech.

![Words signed by age (signing sub-set), coloured by study](figures/scatter_age_signed_ds.png){#fig-signed-age .lightbox fig-align="left"}
